FN-V7DWNPP-2
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 28
Committee: County and Municipal Government Sponsor: Senator Chris Elliott
Analyst: Michael Russo Date: 01/14/2026
Senate Bill 28 as reported by the Committee on County and Municipal Government allows
certain retirees of the Employees' Retirement System (ERS) and the Teachers' Retirement
System (TRS) to return to work without suspension of retirement pay and benefits as sheriff's
deputies, municipal police officers, school bus drivers, and assistant district attorneys, provided
the retiree's annual compensation does not exceed $52,000.
This bill could increase the obligations of state or local agencies, that employ these individuals
by an undetermined amount dependent upon any additional compensation paid to previously
retired employees under the provisions of this bill.
The provisions of this bill shall end December 31, 2030.

FN-V7DWNPP-3
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 28
Committee: Ways and Means General Sponsor: Senator Chris Elliott
Analyst: Michael Russo Date: 02/17/2026
Senate Bill 28 as passed by the Senate would allow certain retirees of the Employees'
Retirement System (ERS) and the Teachers' Retirement System (TRS) to return to work without
suspension of thier retirement allowance as sheriff's deputies, municipal police officers, and
assistant district attorneys, provided the retiree's annual compensation does not exceed $52,000
as provided by this bill.
This bill would also allow certain ERS or TRS retirees to return to work without suspension of
their retirement allowance as school bus drivers, provided their annual compensation does not
exceed the cap set by current law for 2026 ($40,000).
This bill would also extend the sunset of these return-to-work provisions from December 31,
2030, under current law, to December 31, 2032.
These provisions could increase the obligations of state or local agencies that employ these
individuals by an undetermined amount dependent upon any difference in: 1) compensation paid
to these individuals under the provisions of this bill; and 2) compensation otherwise paid under
current law.
